co_pipeline_wall.blurb: A conglomerate cliff on the canyon wall east of Telluride, close to Bridal Veil Falls at roughly 9,000 feet. Nearly all of the 25 routes are bolted sport lines, plus one trad route and one top-rope. The grades start gentle, with a few easy routes and a handful of 5.7 to 5.9 lines to warm up on, then bunch up in the 5.10 and 5.11 range, with a single route in the 5.13 range. Expect pocket pulling on firm stone and long views over the valley. Most routes are one pitch, though a few stretch to three. Helmets are a good idea, because some lines sit below a via ferrata.

co_mongoose_block.blurb: A big, free-standing sandstone boulder in the Snake Pit pocket of Garden of the Gods, Colorado Springs. All 25 problems are bouldering, and the bulk are easy to moderate, from V0 to V4, so it suits beginners and anyone warming up. Above that sits a hard tier running from V6 to V11 for strong climbers. Landings are mostly flat and sandy. Two overhanging aretes are fun at nearly any grade, and sit starts can be added to many problems to make them harder. The rock is solid and the block is chalked up and easy to spot from the trail.
co_mongoose_block.parking_note: Leave the car in the South Garden of the Gods lot; do not park along the road.
co_mongoose_block.approach: Walk north from the south lot on the trail for a short stroll of about a quarter mile. The block is the big boulder on your left.

co_wipeyur_buttress.blurb: A granite buttress in the Devil's Head zone of the Rampart Range, in Colorado's South Platte climbing country. Of the 24 routes, nearly all are bolted sport lines, with one trad route. Grades run from 5.7 up to the 5.13 range, but most of the climbing sits between 5.9 and 5.12, with a strong cluster at 5.12, so it rewards climbers who are comfortable on steeper, harder pitches. Routes are mostly one pitch. The faces look east and southeast, which gives plenty of morning and midday sunshine.

co_j_jabba_buttress.blurb: A sandstone buttress in the East Animas zone, not far from Durango and sitting around 7,000 feet in the La Plata Mountains. Its 24 routes are a blend of 14 sport lines and 10 trad lines, and the rock offers cracks, corners and faces, with some multi-pitch outings. Grades run from 5.7 into the 5.14 range; the middle of the range at 5.9 to 5.12 is well stocked, and a few hard sport lines sit above that. The crack routes are quieter than the busy sport walls nearby, and the east side picks up the morning light.

co_castle_the.blurb: A large granite crag on the northern edge of the South Platte, usually grouped with the Buffalo Creek crags. This is trad country: all 25 routes here are traditionally protected, running up crack systems and plates, and several are multi-pitch lines of up to a few pitches. The grades are mostly 5.10, with a good number at 5.9 and a handful of 5.11s, plus one easy scramble-style route. It is a place for climbers who are happy to place gear and sustain a long day, rather than clip bolts, and many faces nearby remain unclimbed.

co_main_wall_4.blurb: The biggest face on Blob Rock in Boulder Canyon, sitting between the Central Chimney and the Right Gully. It carries more climbs than any other part of the formation: 20 trad routes and 4 bolted ones. Single-pitch lines are roughly 70 to 100 feet tall, and the longer routes go up to three pitches and about 250 feet. Grades range from 5.7 to the low 5.12s, with most routes at 5.9 through 5.11, so it suits climbers comfortable leading traditional gear on granite. A trail zigzags up to the base.
